points.title: What normalisation is
points.must: Organising data into well-structured related tables following the normal forms so each fact is stored once, redundancy is reduced and anomalies are avoided.

points.title: Data redundancy
points.must: The same data stored more than once; it wastes storage and can become inconsistent.

points.title: Update anomaly
points.must: Repeated data must be changed in many rows; missing one makes the data inconsistent — with an example (address in every order).

points.title: Insertion anomaly
points.must: Data cannot be added without other unrelated data — e.g. a new customer cannot be stored before an order.

points.title: Deletion anomaly
points.must: Deleting one record also deletes other needed data — e.g. deleting a customer’s only order loses the customer.

points.title: Benefits of normalisation
points.must: At least two: less redundancy / storage, consistent data (change in one place), no anomalies, easier to maintain.

points.title: Drawbacks
points.must: More tables so queries need joins (can be slower / more complex); some systems denormalise for speed.

points.title: Order of the normal forms
points.must: UNF → 1NF → 2NF → 3NF; each form includes the rules of the one before (staircase diagram).

points.title: Rule of 1NF
points.must: Atomic values (one value per cell), no repeating groups, a primary key so each record is unique.

points.title: Rule of 2NF
points.must: In 1NF and every non-key field depends on the whole primary key — no partial dependencies.

points.title: Rule of 3NF
points.must: In 2NF and no non-key field depends on another non-key field — no transitive dependencies; “the key, the whole key and nothing but the key”.

points.title: Key terms
points.must: Atomic value, repeating group, composite key, functional dependency (A → B) — each with an example.

points.title: Full, partial and transitive dependency
points.must: One example of each, e.g. (StudentID, SubjectID) → Mark; StudentID → StudentName; Class → ClassTeacher; which form each breaks.

points.title: Single-field key
points.must: A 1NF table with a single-field primary key is automatically in 2NF because a partial dependency needs a composite key.
